title: Hydrodynamic magnetotransport in a GaAs Corbino geometry
authors: A. D. Levin, A. S. Jaroshevich, Z. D. Kvon, V. A. Chitta, M. S. Aksenov, D. V. Dmitriev, A. K. Bakarov, G. M. Gusev
abstract: We report the observation of positive magnetoresistance in high-mobility GaAs Corbino devices. Over a broad intermediate-temperature range, the resistance exhibits a quadratic dependence on perpendicular magnetic field. We analyze the data within hydrodynamic theories of magnetotransport in the Corbino geometry, which describe the crossover between the diffusive and viscous regimes, including finite-slip boundary conditions appropriate for current-penetrable contacts. The extracted relaxation rates are consistent with an approximately $T^2$ temperature dependence of the electron-electron scattering contribution. The extracted viscous relaxation parameters are consistent with those obtained from Hall-bar measurements. Comparison with theory indicates that the observed magnetoresistance is predominantly governed by the bulk hydrodynamic response, while finite slip modifies the Stokes--Ohm crossover quantitatively and the field-dependent boundary voltage provides a separate correction. These results show that Corbino magnetotransport can serve as a complementary bulk-sensitive probe of viscous electron flow.
summary: This work reports on the observation and theoretical analysis of positive magnetoresistance in GaAs Corbino devices. By applying hydrodynamic theories, the authors successfully separate the bulk viscous transport contribution from boundary effects. The findings establish Corbino magnetotransport as a sensitive, bulk-sensitive probe for studying viscous electron flow in 2DEGs.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of positive magnetoresistance observed in high-mobility GaAs Corbino devices by analyzing hydrodynamic magnetotransport.
main_result: The observed magnetoresistance is predominantly governed by the bulk hydrodynamic response, which can be analyzed by fitting the data to theoretical models incorporating finite-slip boundary conditions.
method: The authors analyze magnetoresistance measurements ($\Delta R \propto B^2$) using hydrodynamic theories that describe the crossover between diffusive and viscous electron flow in an annular geometry.
model_or_system: The physical system is a GaAs Corbino geometry (2DEG in an annulus). The model uses hydrodynamic theories to describe current flow, incorporating finite-slip boundary conditions at current-penetrable contacts.
key_observables: Positive magnetoresistance ($\Delta R$) exhibiting a quadratic dependence on the perpendicular magnetic field ($B^2$), and the temperature dependence of the extracted relaxation rates.
important_parameters: The analysis spans regimes from the diffusive limit to the hydrodynamic Stokes limit, characterized by geometric ratios and temperature-dependent scattering rates.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the hydrodynamic description and accounts for boundary effects (finite slip and field-dependent contact voltage) as separate corrections to the bulk response.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic geometries, magnetoresistance vs. $B^2$ plots, and temperature/radius dependence of the magnetoresistance coefficient ($\alpha$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from presenting the experimental observation of quadratic magnetoresistance in Corbino devices to applying detailed hydrodynamic models that account for the crossover between different transport regimes and boundary corrections.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state transport, the detailed modeling of non-equilibrium, viscous, and hydrodynamic flow in mesoscopic geometries provides a rich example of continuum physics applicable to open quantum systems or complex many-body dynamics.
